newsitem.title: FRANCE: French unemployment to hit 13 pct in 1997 - INSEE.
newsitem.headline: French unemployment to hit 13 pct in 1997 - INSEE.

text.p: French unemployment is likely to rise to 13 percent of the workforce next spring, national statistics institute INSEE said on Tuesday.
It said it expected the economy to lose some 100,000 jobs in 1996 after the creation of 130,000 in 1995 and 210,000 in 1994.
French unemployment is currently at a record 12.6 percent.
In its semi-annual economic note, INSEE raised slightly its prediction for 1996 gross domestic product (GDP) growth to 1.3 percent from 1.2 percent.
The revised forecast matches government predictions for 1996 growth.
Year-on-year GDP growth at the end of June 1997 should be 2.5 percent, INSEE said.
The French government is counting on an economic recovery next year to boost growth and help France cut its deficit in preparation for European Economic and Monetary Union in 1999.
INSEE predicts that first-half growth next year in European Union countries will reach an average annual rate of 2.5 percent.

Exports should rise due to an increase in Airbus deliveries and strong worldwide demand for manufactured goods and should result in France's first half trade surplus exceeding its level in the first six months of 1996, INSEE said.
The institute said tax cuts and low inflation of 1.6 percent year-on-year at the end of June 1997 should lead to a 1.2 percent gain in household purchasing power.
But consumer consumption is expected to rise only 0.3 percent in the second half of 1996, and the same amount in the first half of 1997.
Business investment should rise 2.4 percent in the last six months of 1996 and 0.9 percent in the first half of 1997, INSEE said.
Industrial production was likely to rise more strongly, posting a four percent gain year on year at the end of June, 1997.
